thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered for routing-policy anomaly (sev2). Summary: unexpected spill of hosted traffic into Dedicated pool causing latency + errors for a subset of tenants. Affected tenants: tenant-42, tenant-88. Auto-detection flagged capacity-tier mismatch and >50% error increase. Paging @alex (eng-oncall) for live mitigation.

alex: ack — on it. can someone drop any immediate logs / suspect config? I’ll start with the routing decision trace.

maria: seeing a bunch of fallback decisions where policy engine returned model_variant=dense-dedicated even though tenant has reserved_hosted=true. looks like the tenant isolation check is being skipped when pool_utilization>0.85.

devin: pasting a couple of lines from the router logs:
```
2026-03-15T18:40:12.123Z ROUTER [req=0x7f9] tenant=tenant-42 route_eval: fallback_allowed=true pool=hosted pool_util=0.92 -> selected_pool=dedicated_variant:dense-dedicated
2026-03-15T18:40:12.124Z ROUTER [req=0x7f9] tenant=tenant-42 isolation_check=SKIPPED reason=overutilized
```

devin: also dumping the active fallback rule from the live config:
```
{
  "fallback": {
    "enable": true,
    "max_hosted_util_pct": 85,
    "allow_dedicated_fallback": true,
    "tenant_isolation": "soft"
  }
}
```

alex: ok — looks like "tenant_isolation":"soft" is the problem here. It treats reserved_hosted as advisory and allows dedicated fallback if util > threshold. That explains the tenant leak. immediate mitigation: set `allow_dedicated_fallback=false` for the global policy and apply a temporary override to force hosted-only routing for the affected tenants. Doing that now.

alex: running admin command to patch policy: `curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/config/routing/policy/override -d '{"allow_dedicated_fallback":false}' -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN"`

alex: command returned 200 and a policy version bump: v2026-03-15-1820. Router nodes should pick up in ~30s. Confirming on a few nodes:
```
node-router-03: policy v2026-03-15-1820 loaded
node-router-07: policy v2026-03-15-1820 loaded
```

maria: good — I'm seeing the routing decisions flip back to hosted for tenant-42. errors dropping in metrics.

sam: support update: customer tenant-42 (account-icf) filed ticket #6789 complaining of 502s and 10s latency spikes starting ~18:39 UTC. I told them we have a mitigation in place and that we're investigating cause. they asked if any data left dedicated cluster — not yet reported, but they want confirmation.

alex: can we confirm no data egress? devin, any logs showing requests hitting dedicated that would indicate request/state mismatch?

devin: quick grep: I see requests forwarded to dedicated backend for tenant-42 between 18:39:58 and 18:41:30, approx 1.5k requests. No sign of model state writes (we don't write persistent KV during inference) but KV cache entries were populated in dedicated node logs — likely cold-caches filled. No PII or SA data written.

alex: noted. we'll include that in customer note: calls hit dedicated, no persistent data was written to disk; transient KV populated. sam please draft a customer-safe message: "We saw routed requests to our dedicated pool transiently; behavior has been reverted; no customer data was written to disk; we’ll follow up with a full incident report."

sam: drafting now and will post to ticket + status page draft.

liz: for follow-up, we should flip tenant_isolation to "hard" for reserved_hosted tenants and add a canary rule for the policy change. also suggest an automated test that simulates hosted util spikes and verifies that reserved tenants are never evicted.

alex: agreed. immediate post-incident actions: 1) revert override only after we validate stable metrics for 1 hour. 2) open PR to change default tenant_isolation semantics for reserved_hosted -> hard. 3) add unit/integration tests to routing engine and a live canary job. 4) run a cross-team postmortem.

incident-bot: Incident record created: INC-2026-0315-07. Severity: 2. Impacted customers: tenant-42, tenant-88. Mitigation: global override applied to disable dedicated fallback; targeted tenant overrides applied. Assigned owners: alex (oncall), devin (infra lead), maria (sre).

alex: handing off to maria for overnight monitoring. I’ll add my notes to the incident doc and then go offline. maria — please watch the error budget and latency for those tenants and escalate to eng-oncall if anything resurfaces.

maria: taking handoff. logging into shift tracker and will maintain heartbeat checks every 15m for next 4 hours.

sam: customer message posted and ticket updated. ticket link: https://support.redwood.ai/tickets/6789 (internal).

alex: thanks everyone. postmortem trigger: yes (sev2 + customer impact). we’ll run RCA and propose policy change. set a follow-up meeting in #postmortems for tomorrow 10:00 PT.

liz: quick note: add a config validation in the admin UI to warn when tenant_isolation=soft and allow_dedicated_fallback=true with reserved_hosted tenants present. that could have caught this earlier.

alex: +1. adding that to action items.

incident-bot: Next update scheduled in 30m or on owner comment.
